text: This course built two things in parallel: evaluating an AI system before shipping, and watching, documenting, and responding to it once it's live. The capstone puts both halves together, end to end, for one real feature you choose.
The feature can be simple — a support-ticket triage assistant, a summarizer, a small RAG Q&A tool, a classifier. What matters is real inputs and outputs you can actually run calls against.
An eval dataset of fifteen to twenty test cases. A monitoring setup with logging and a dashboard view. One incident response plan for a realistic failure. A model card documenting what you built.
The most common way a capstone goes wrong is picking something too ambitious to finish. A five-question eval set you actually build beats a fifty-question one you never complete.
Every deliverable pulls from a specific earlier lesson on purpose — this isn't new material, it's assembly. Next up: actually building the pipeline, deliverable by deliverable.
